findings.reason: The protected SQL solution executes two SELECT queries using COUNT(*) and LIKE predicates ('% bull %', '% bear %') combined with UNION ALL. This directly counts files containing at least one space-bounded occurrence of 'bull' or 'bear'. The query executes in O(S) time where S is total text character length and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

Using literal spaces around the word ('% bull %' and '% bear %') strictly enforces space boundaries, excluding embedded words (bullet, bears), punctuation-adjacent occurrences (bull.), and boundary positions. COUNT(*) per query counts qualifying files once.
Scanning text content of length S takes O(S) time across the table. Output consists of exactly two rows using O(1) space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts Files table and returns word and count columns for 'bull' and 'bear'.

The approach accurately details space-bounded LIKE pattern matching, COUNT(*) aggregation, UNION ALL combination, and O(S) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover conditional aggregation overhead, regex word-boundary pitfalls, token splitting risks, file-level deduplication, dual-match rows, boundary rejection, and zero-count row guarantees.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical UNION ALL LIKE pattern query with SHA-256 digests 774e26ef907956fd40e7b5a55b0f949cb0fa1d317835afe2f1250e259cfc18fd and fe9931b9413e5dca7811b6b9271b9e4cd4c8f0d36d1ac4c7b4483a7bb3506014. Verified submission remains untouched.
